outputs: APPARATUS FAULT FOUND AND FIXED IN THE HARNESS (not in source): HUD.update() clears the 2D overlay exactly once when hidden and then returns, while Menus.update() keeps painting the intro wash into that same canvas every frame. Calling hud.__hide() while the title card is still live therefore stamps 陽炎 on a black field into every subsequent screenshot, permanently. The first ablation run photographed two frames that way (whole-frame luma p50 3.4) before the frames were checked. The rerun starts the game, cancels the intro, leaves the HUD visible to clear itself, asserts _title < 0 and _titleA = _introWash = 0, and only then hides; it also aborts if abl-h-base whole-frame p50 < 40. Worth carrying into tools/capture.mjs — it is one reordered call away from silently ruining a whole review set. Owner of the underlying behaviour: src/ui/HUD.js.

FINDING 1 (blocker, 'no readable cast shadow on the plaza') — SYMPTOM CONFIRMED, MECHANISM DISPROVED. The critic's own labelled hypothesis is correct and this is not a CSM fault. Ablating the ambient/probe/rim to zero on hero and re-shooting (abl-h-noamb) makes lantern-, post- and fence-shaped bars appear across the plaza immediately. Differentially, with kagShadowFade forced negative: at full rig the plaza band (0,900,2532,270) is 30.8% cast shadow, lit p50 46.0 against shadowed 33.4, a factor of 1.38; with the ambient zeroed the same band is 34.2% cast shadow, lit p50 19.7 against shadowed 8.8, a factor of 2.24. The shadow map reaches the plaza; the ambient floor squashes its contrast.

FINDING 1 — THE CRITIC MEASURED THE SHADOW AND CALLED IT THE GROUND. Its eleven-box scan at y=0.80 reproduces on this rig to about one code value (33.2/53.1/37.0/40.4/41.5/45.3/54.3/17.1/75.9/62.9/60.1 against the filed 33.4/52.9/37.4/39.4/41.5/45.4/54.4/17.3/75.7/62.6/60.1). Removing the shadow term brightens boxes x=0.10 through x=0.58 by +7.0 to +11.2 luma each and leaves x=0.66..0.90 unchanged: seven of the eleven boxes used to argue 'there is no elongated dark structure anywhere on the plane' are themselves inside cast shadow. The metric also cannot work here by construction — when more than half the sampled line is shadowed, the scan median is itself a shadowed value, so no box can read 30% below it. The critic's own box (152,1006,152,59), described as 'shaded plaza', is 84.6% cast shadow.

FINDING 1 — WHY THE CONTRAST IS ONLY 1.38x, AND THE Lighting.js DEFECT THAT HID IT. ambientReport tracked key/probe/hemi and omitted this.rim, a scene-wide DirectionalLight with castShadow = false carrying 0.1482 of luminous irradiance — a third of the stated fill again, and present inside the cast shadow. Counted, the fill is 0.5937 against a key of 0.3960, i.e. 1.50x the key, not the 1.125x the three-term report implied. On a horizontal plane the best a shadow can then do is 1 + key/fill = 1.67x; measured 1.38x, so a further ~0.45 of unshadowed pedestal (god rays, bloom, lantern pool) sits on top. Fixed: rim and fill are now reported. The rim's level was NOT changed — it is cool (B/R 1.910) and serves §5.10, and lowering it unverified is exactly the move this project keeps punishing.

FINDING 0 (blocker, 'every shadowed surface is warm brown') — THE FILL IS COOL AND IS ARRIVING; ITS HUE WAS WRONG AT SOURCE. Fill-only on hero's shaded plaza (abl-h-nokey, key and point lights zeroed) measures meanRGB 18.0/22.1/25.1, B/R 1.394 — cool, and 79% of that pixel's luminance (removing the ambient takes its p50 from 29.6 to 6.3). Root cause found in Sky.js: SHADOW_FILL_MAX_RB was 0.52, which is §5 #4a6b8f's R/B read off its sRGB bytes (74/143), compared against Color.r/Color.b which three stores in the linear working space where the same hex is 0.2493. The ceiling was 2.08x too warm, the live fill measured 0.4431 against it, and the one clamp whose whole job is to hold the fill on §5 had never fired. The rebalance also squared its own correction (scaling red by s and blue by 1/s moves the ratio by s^2, landing on target^2/rb). Both fixed; verified numerically: skyColor R/B 0.4432 -> 0.2493 at luminance 0.2589 -> 0.2589 unchanged, hemiIntensity 1.0197 -> 1.0198, delivered fill B/R 1.839 -> 2.598 at luminous irradiance 0.4454 -> 0.4454. The level is untouched, which is what HANDOFF open item 2 requires.

FINDING 0 — HANDOFF OPEN ITEM 2's NAMED MECHANISM IS DISPROVED. Removing both eaters at runtime — Materials.js aoMapIntensity set to 0 on every material in the scene, and PostFX.js uAoStrength set to 0 — moves the fill-only shaded plaza from meanRGB 18.0/22.1/25.1 p50 21.0 to 18.6/22.9/25.9 p50 21.6: +2.9%, or a signed mean of -0.35 luma over the plaza band against a frame-to-frame noise floor where 77-87% of pixels already differ by more than 0.5. The ablation demonstrably applied (the frames are not byte-identical). Corroborated at source: PostFX's SSAO block is 'c *= occTint * k' on the whole composited colour, not on indirectDiffuse, so it cannot preferentially eat the fill — and its own comment already records uIndirect = 1.000 on every ground pixel, lit and shadowed alike. 'Roughly a tenth of the budgeted fill survives' does not reproduce on hero's plaza. The materials and postfx owners should stop looking there.

FINDING 0 — TARGET (a) IS PHYSICALLY UNREACHABLE, MEASURED TWO WAYS. Box (760,515,127,47) must go from B/R 0.578 to >= 1.30. (i) The surface is weathered cedar, PAL.cedar #5a4436 / cedarWarm #7a5c42 / cedarHeart #3b2a1e, linear albedo B/R 0.361-0.49; a Lambertian pixel is albedo x illuminant, so >= 1.30 needs an illuminant at linear B/R >= 3.6 — i.e. essentially pure #4a6b8f (4.007) with no key, probe, rim, bounce or air. (ii) Photographed under exactly that (abl-h-fill45: hemisphere forced to #4a6b8f at matched irradiance, everything else zeroed, fog off) the box still measures B/R 0.378, 0.355 excluding its bright pixels — because the box straddles the haiden's lit paper lanterns and emissive shoji panels, which no lighting change touches. The same shot puts the flagstone plaza box at B/R 4.066, so targets (b) and (c) have physical headroom and only (a) does not.

FINDING 10 (minor, near/mid haze) — ATTRIBUTION DISPROVED. Removing the aerial perspective ENTIRELY from the sun frame (abl-s-nofog: uFogDensity, uFogAirDensity and scene.fog.density all zeroed) leaves both of the finding's own boxes where they were. Mid band (1266,585,506,23): meanRGB 233.7/221.0/190.2 saturation 0.188 p50 226.3 with fog, and 233.7/221.0/190.2 saturation 0.188 p50 226.2 without it. Near torii post (1823,410,152,293): detail 1.42 -> 1.44, p50 110.8 -> 109.6. Mid post detail 0.98 -> 0.98. The haze draws essentially none of those pixels — at 30-60 m its opacity is about 0.12 and the surface behind it is already at 226, so it is mixing a value into an identical value. Targets (a) saturation >= 0.28 / p50 <= 205 and (b) near-post detail >= 4.5 are therefore NOT reachable from Sky.js. The wash is the additive god-ray and bloom pass, which PostFX applies before exposure; abl-s-nopost is the paired frame. Owner: src/render/PostFX.js. Consequently the fogParams ramp (start 6, heightFalloff 26, airDensity 0.00098) was deliberately NOT retuned: the measurement gives no mandate, and thinning it would make the haiden facade — which is 83% aerial perspective — darker and warmer, i.e. move finding 0 backwards.

AERIAL PERSPECTIVE IS NEUTRAL GREY, WHICH §5 FORBIDS — and it is a finding-0 lever, not a finding-10 one. uFogColor reads live as (0.3177,0.3104,0.3153), linear B/R 0.992, against the ladder's own authored #97a6bd at 1.644; at magic hour airW = 1 so the authored value is fully replaced by the dome's anti-sunward horizon. That is honest physics for a 26-air-mass path and the wrong sample to paint the first forty metres with. Worse, fogCol keyed on view elevation alone, so every ground-directed ray reached that grey at every distance while uFogTopColor (linear B/R 1.634) was reachable only by looking up. Measured share of pixel luminance: 83% on the haiden facade at ~34 m (p50 30.9 -> 5.1 with fog off), 14% on hero's shaded plaza at ~12 m (29.6 -> 25.4), 2% on torii's plaza at a few metres (40.4 -> 39.6), and 0% on the sun frame's mid band. Fixed by blending the near/mid field onto uFogTopColor and converging on the horizon only as the ray goes optically thick, so past f = 0.45 the expression is byte-identical to round 8 and the far-silhouette invariant holds by construction. Note the fog is NOT what warms the shadows: removing it makes hero's shaded plaza box slightly WARMER, B/R 0.822 -> 0.801, because the grey air is marginally cooler than the pixel it sits on. It does raise shadow readability a little — the plaza's shadowed/unshadowed scan ratio goes 1.52 -> 1.61 with fog removed.

FINDING 5 (major, sun disc) — THE DISC IS ALREADY FULLY CLIPPED AND CANNOT BE LIFTED. With uSunE read back at 163.083, the core's scene-linear radiance is uSunE x Fex x gain = 163.083 x (0.4996,0.2106,0.0338) x 1.8 = (146.6, 61.8, 9.93). At the composite's railed effExposure 1.500 every channel enters ACES between 24.8 and 367, so all three saturate: the disc is white by construction. Three of the four stated targets are therefore unreachable. (a) p50 >= 254 forces, with R = G = 255, B >= 241, i.e. B/R >= 0.945, while (b) demands B/R <= 0.80 on the same 30x29 box. (c) needs core p50 >= 278 in an 8-bit frame once the surround is pinned within +/-12 of 225.9. (b)'s annulus saturation >= 0.20 is capped at 1 - 208.4/255 = 0.183 even with red fully clipped, because its blue is scene-linear 0.410 and can only be added to; roughly 44% of that blue is the bloom/god-ray pedestal, which is PostFX's.

FINDING 5 — THE REAL DEFECT IS THAT THE KNEE FLATTENS THE WHOLE AUREOLE, AND IT IS FIXABLE. SKY_KNEE is an order-4 ceiling, which for y >> ceil returns luminance exactly ceil. Evaluating the dome fragment on the live grade, pre-knee luminance is 8.522 at 2 degrees off the sun and 4.846 at 10 degrees, and both leave the knee at 0.4600. The frame agrees: radially profiling phone-sun-r15.png about its peak at (1530,530) gives luma 230.4/230.3/230.2/230.0/229.7/229.3/228.9 at r = 48/54/60/66/72/78/84 px — 1.5 code values over 36 px. That flat plate is the critic's 'no wide falloff, it stops after about 60 px'. Separately, the drawn disc is 5.96 px of radius at the sun framing (22.5 px per degree), so the ~48 px blob the frame shows is bloom, not disc — hence 'bokeh smudge'. Fixed by drawing the disc at SUN_DISC_SCALE 3.0 (0.795 deg radius, the size Lighting.js:_computeSplits already prices its penumbra at with spread = 0.055, 'artistic sun size ~3 degrees not 0.53'), and by widening the Fex-tinted glare skirt from 2.4 to 5.96 degrees at gain 0.006 -> 0.024 so the plateau becomes a monotone falloff.
